fulica-atra.titleZh: 白骨顶的图片曾经出过什么问题？（已修复）
fulica-atra.titleEn: What happened to the Eurasian Coot photos? (Fixed)
fulica-atra.bodyZh:
AI 调查结论

曾经的首图（现已撤下）里，主体其实是一只雀鹰在扑抓水面的白骨顶，白骨顶在背景里。iNaturalist 上这条观察（90178562）的首图票数最高，旧算法按“首图”取图才会出现这种情况。

修复分三步：① 改为优先使用物种的策展默认图（default_photo），并加入人工覆盖表兜底——现在首图是一张清晰的白骨顶（照片 123574818）；② 2026-10-21 复核时发现那张雀鹰照片仍排在画廊第 2 位，已从素材列表中移除（R2 旧文件保留备查、不再展示）；③ 同日补充 1 张清晰的白骨顶亲鸟带雏（iNaturalist 观察 17125901，Geoffrey Cox，CC BY-NC），现在共 5 张（1/3/4/5/6），首图仍是原来那张清晰的白骨顶。

这张观察在 iNaturalist 上仍是白骨顶（Fulica atra）：雀鹰只是画面主体，观察记录的是被扑抓的白骨顶。问题出在“取观察首图”的旧逻辑，不是物种标注。

同一物种的不同角度、季节、雌雄或幼鸟差异也很大。如果你仍看到旧图，多半是浏览器 / Service Worker 缓存，可用无痕窗口或清站点数据后重试。
fulica-atra.bodyEn:
AI investigation

The old first photo (now retired) actually showed a Eurasian Sparrowhawk grabbing a coot on the water, with the coot in the background. That observation (90178562) had the most-voted first photo on iNaturalist, and the old algorithm picked the observation’s first photo.

The fix had three steps: (1) prefer the species’ curated default photo and keep a manual override fallback — the current first photo is a clear coot (photo 123574818); (2) during a 2026-10-21 review we found the sparrowhawk photo was still in slot 2 of the gallery, so it has now been removed from the media list (the old R2 object is kept for auditing but no longer displayed); (3) on the same day we added a clear photo of an adult with chicks (iNaturalist obs 17125901, Geoffrey Cox, CC BY-NC), so the gallery now has 5 photos (1/3/4/5/6), with the original clear coot still as the first image.

The observation is still identified as a coot (Fulica atra) on iNaturalist: the sparrowhawk was only the subject of the photo, while the record is the coot being grabbed. The problem was the old “take the observation’s first photo” logic, not the species identification.

A species can also look quite different by angle, season, sex or age. If you still see the old photo, it is most likely a browser / Service Worker cache — try a private window or clear site data.

pica-serica.titleZh: 喜鹊的图片换过吗？为什么？
pica-serica.titleEn: Have the Oriental Magpie photos changed? Why?
pica-serica.bodyZh:
AI 调查结论

喜鹊原有 5 张图，其中 3 张不适合做认鸟练习，已停用并补入 3 张新图；现在展示的是原第 2、4 张 + 新增第 6、7、8 张，共 5 张。

8 张图一览（编号 = 加入顺序）：
1. 原图 1（iNaturalist 观察 253827966）— 已停用：主体与喜鹊不符
2. 原图 2（121031511）— 保留
3. 原图 3（38753010）— 已停用：画面模糊
4. 原图 4（121031510）— 保留
5. 原图 5（394144078）— 已停用：羽色异常，与典型喜鹊差异过大
6. 新图 6（205466820，CC0）— 新增
7. 新图 7（155853528，CC BY-NC）— 新增
8. 新图 8（384500520，CC BY-NC）— 新增

需要说明的是：这 8 条观察在 iNaturalist 上都被标注为喜鹊（Pica serica）。问题出在源站素材本身的质量与标注，而不是本站抓取时认错了物种。旧图仍保留在服务器上备查，只是不再展示。

感谢在「大众评审」指出问题的朋友——每一条反馈我们都会人工核对；确认有误的素材会停用并补充替换，同时在下方更新日志留痕。

开发者言

对于图一（之前考题中出现的图）我其实困惑过：它是喜鹊吗？但是没做进一步查证，以为是白化喜鹊或者是幼鸟。后续一直在试图完善项目的各种功能，也未及时找人求证。目前图一已经停用，并且对图三（模糊）、图五（白色浅色，疑似也是误标）也做了停用，然后额外新增了三张图。
pica-serica.bodyEn:
AI investigation

The Oriental Magpie used to have 5 photos; 3 of them were unsuitable for identification practice. They are retired and replaced with 3 new photos. The gallery now shows original #2 and #4 plus new #6, #7 and #8 (5 in total).

All 8 photos (numbering = order added):
1. Original 1 (iNaturalist obs 253827966) — retired: the subject is not a magpie
2. Original 2 (121031511) — kept
3. Original 3 (38753010) — retired: blurry
4. Original 4 (121031510) — kept
5. Original 5 (394144078) — retired: atypical plumage, too different from a typical magpie
6. New 6 (205466820, CC0) — added
7. New 7 (155853528, CC BY-NC) — added
8. New 8 (384500520, CC BY-NC) — added

All 8 observations are labelled Pica serica on iNaturalist. The problem was the quality/labelling of the source material, not a species misidentification on our side. The old files are kept on the server for auditing, but are no longer displayed.

Thanks to the person who reported this in Public Review — every report is checked manually; confirmed problems are retired and replaced, with a note in the changelog below.

Developer's note

I had doubts about image 1 (the one that appeared in earlier quizzes) — is it really a magpie? — but I did not verify it further and assumed it was a leucistic magpie or a juvenile. I kept working on other features and did not ask anyone to confirm in time. Image 1 is now retired; image 3 (blurry) and image 5 (pale/white, also suspected to be mislabelled) have been retired as well, and three new photos have been added.
